items.stem: (a) Describe the vacuum bell jar experiment to show that sound needs a medium to propagate? (b) Based on this observation, what type of wave is sound? (c) Draw a well-labelled diagram of the experimental setup?
items.answer: (a) An experiment to demonstrate that sound requires a material medium is the vacuum bell jar experiment. The setup consists of an electric bell suspended inside an airtight glass bell jar, which is placed on a base connected to a vacuum pump. Initially, when the bell is switched on, its ringing sound is clearly heard because the jar is filled with air. As the vacuum pump gradually removes the air from the jar, the loudness of the sound steadily decreases, even though the hammer continues to strike the gong. Eventually, when a near vacuum is created, the sound becomes almost inaudible. (b) This observation proves that sound is a mechanical wave. Unlike electromagnetic waves, sound cannot travel through empty space. It fundamentally relies on the collisions of particles in a physical medium, such as a solid, liquid, or gas, to propagate and transfer energy.

items.stem: During a science exhibition, a group of ninth graders set up a long metal slinky on a smooth table. One student pushed and pulled one end of the slinky in quick succession while the other end was held firmly. The visitors observed bands of closely packed coils moving towards the fixed end, followed by regions where the coils were spread far apart. To show that the metal coils themselves were not travelling from one end to the other, a student tied a small red ribbon to one of the middle coils and asked the audience to observe its motion. QUESTIONS: (a) What do the closely packed coils and the spread-out coils represent in a sound wave travelling through air? (b) Describe the motion of the red ribbon as the disturbance passes through the slinky. (c) What specific type of wave is demonstrated in this exhibition? (d) How does this slinky activity explain the concept that sound is a mechanical wave?
items.answer: (a) The closely packed coils represent compressions (regions of higher density), and the spread-out coils represent rarefactions (regions of lower density) in a sound wave. (b) The red ribbon does not travel to the end of the slinky. It only oscillates back and forth parallel to the direction of the disturbance, about its own position of rest. (c) This demonstrates a longitudinal wave, where the particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation. (d) The activity shows that a disturbance requires a physical material (the slinky) to travel from one point to another. Since sound also requires a material medium to propagate and cannot travel in a vacuum, it is classified as a mechanical wave.
